learningObjective: Precisely define the goal of KV cache quantization in LLM serving.

canonicalClaims.claim: KV cache quantization targets the per-request Key/Value tensors accumulated across decode steps, reducing GPU memory footprint (enabling longer contexts / larger batches) and, when the attention kernel supports it, reducing attention memory bandwidth.
conditions: The attention implementation supports reading quantized KVs.
The workload is memory-limited at the KV cache axis (typical for long context or high concurrency).
nonImplications: Does not imply zero accuracy cost.
Does not target model weights or input embeddings.

misconceptions.claim: KV cache quantization reduces attention compute by using INT8 Tensor Cores.
misconceptions.whyWrong: KV compute (K^T Q, softmax, PV) is a small fraction of attention FLOPs; the target is memory footprint and bandwidth.

misconceptions.claim: KV cache quantization is another name for model weight quantization applied to the attention projection layers.
misconceptions.whyWrong: KV cache is per-request runtime data; model weight quantization is offline.

misconceptions.claim: KV cache quantization compresses input token embeddings before they enter the transformer.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Input embeddings are separate; KV cache is generated during decoding by K/V projections.

misconceptions.claim: KV cache quantization has no memory-footprint benefit at batch=1; only at batch>1.
misconceptions.whyWrong: At batch=1 with long context (e.g., 32K), KV cache can occupy the majority of GPU memory; quantization is beneficial even at batch=1.

implementationFacts: TensorRT-LLM supports FP8 and INT8 KV cache quantization.
vLLM added INT8 / FP8 KV cache options over 2024.
PagedAttention already reduces KV memory fragmentation; quantization is orthogonal and complementary.
performanceScenarios: LLaMA-70B at 32K context: FP16 KV cache per request ~40 GB; INT8 halves this.
